name: Ventral posterolateral nucleus (VPL)
summary: The somatosensory relay for the body. The medial lemniscus and spinothalamic tract end here in a somatotopic map (leg lateral, arm medial, with the face taking over in the adjacent VPM), and third-order neurons project through the posterior limb of the internal capsule to the postcentral gyrus. A small infarct of the thalamogeniculate branches confined to VPL and VPM produces the pure sensory stroke, and its recovery phase may bring the intractable burning pain of the thalamic syndrome.

anatomy.location: Posterior part of the ventral tier of the lateral thalamus, lateral to the VPM and medial to the internal capsule, beneath the lateral posterior nucleus and in front of the pulvinar.

efferents.via: posterior limb of the internal capsule

function: Relay of discriminative touch, vibration, proprioception, pain and temperature from the contralateral body to the primary somatosensory cortex.

bestView.label: posterolateral thalamus beside the posterior limb of the internal capsule
VPL lateral to VPM in the ventral tier

imaging.normalAppearance: Not distinguishable from the rest of the thalamus on routine MRI; the MIAL thalamic nuclei mesh in this atlas outlines the ventral posterior group. Lacunes here sit in the posterolateral thalamus next to the internal capsule.

pathology.finding: Small restricted-diffusion lesion in the posterolateral thalamus.
Lateral thalamic infarct including VPL, VPM and sometimes the internal capsule (sensorimotor stroke) and the pulvinar.

lesionEffects.mechanism: Deafferentation and reorganization of the ventral posterior nuclei
Small lesion at the VPL–VPM border where hand and mouth representations are adjacent

examination: All sensory modalities on the opposite body compared with the face
Allodynia and hyperpathia in the affected limbs
pearls: Numbness of the hand and the corner of the mouth together (cheiro-oral) is a tiny lateral thalamic lesion
Thalamic pain is delayed: warn stroke patients with sensory loss to report new burning pain
